title: Events Log & Diagnostics
subtitle: A running, read-only history of everything APRS Command decoded and did, plus live RF health diagnostics for troubleshooting.
in_this_chapter: Opening the Events Log from the View menu
Filtering by category, severity, and callsign
RF Diagnostics: the live link scoreboard
Where the log files live on disk
Troubleshooting a quiet or unhealthy link

blocks.h1: What This Is / What It Is For

blocks.p: The __Events Log__ is APRS Command's running record of what the app has been doing: packets it decoded, stations it saw, ports that connected or dropped, alerts that fired, and messages that came and went. When something looks off — a radio link that went quiet, a beacon that never appeared, a port that will not stay open — the events log is the first place to look. It is a read-only history, so opening it and reading it never puts anything on the air.

Alongside it, the **RF Diagnostics** tool gives you a live scoreboard of your radio link: packet counts, duplicates, unique stations, and warnings about noisy paths or over-eager beacons. Between the two, you can answer "is my station actually hearing traffic, and is everything healthy?" without guessing.

callout.label: Transmit-safe
callout.text: Both the Events Log and RF Diagnostics only observe and report. APRS Command is receive-first and transmit-disabled by default — the **TX Disabled** badge in the title bar stays put — and nothing in these two tools changes that.

blocks.p: The events log lives on the **View** menu. Open it from **View ▸ Events**. It opens in its own floating window titled `APRS Command — Events`, so you can leave it open on a second monitor while you work the map.

steps: The window opens showing the __Decoded Event Log__ — a scrolling list with a filter row across the top and a running count reading `Decoded events: N`.

blocks.screenshot: The Events window: a one-line description strip, a filter row (a Search events box, a Callsign/source box, and three dropdowns for category, severity, and event type), a Clear button at top right, and the scrolling event list below.

blocks.p: Each row lays out the essentials in columns, left to right: the __timestamp__, the __severity__, the __category__, the __event type__, the __callsign or source__, and a plain-language __summary__. A second line underneath carries the __details__ when there are any.

rows: Which part of the app it came from (see the category list below).
The specific thing that happened, e.g. `StationCreated`, `PortDisconnected`, `AlertTriggered`.
The station or feed the event relates to, when one applies.
A readable one-line summary, with extra detail on the line beneath.

blocks.p: The filter row lets you cut a long log down to what you care about. Everything updates as you type or choose — there is no separate Apply button.

bullets: **Search events** — free-text match against the summary, details, and notes. Type part of a message and the list narrows.
**Callsign/source** — show only rows tied to a particular station or feed (for example your own call, or `gpsd`).
**Category dropdown** — defaults to `All`; pick one category to focus on (for example `Port` or `Alert`).
**Severity dropdown** — defaults to `All`; pick `Warning`, `Error`, or `Critical` to surface only problems.
**Event type dropdown** — defaults to `All`; narrow to one exact event, such as `PacketTransmitBlocked`.

callout.label: Find problems fast
callout.text: Set the severity dropdown to `Warning` (or higher) and leave everything else on `All`. What remains is the short list of things the app thought were worth flagging.

blocks.p: Every entry is tagged with one category so you can tell at a glance which subsystem it came from. The categories are:

bullets: `Packet` — raw and parsed packet activity
`Station` — stations created, updated, or expired
`Object` — APRS objects created, updated, or killed
`Weather` — weather reports and weather-station updates
`Message` — messages received, sent, acknowledged, or rejected
`Bulletin` — bulletins received
`GPS` — position/fix updates from a GPS source
`Port` — serial/TNC port connect, disconnect, and errors
`AprsIs` — APRS-IS internet feed connect/disconnect
`RF` — radio-link events
`Beacon` — beacons generated (and, when enabled, transmitted)
`IGate` — I-Gate candidate detection and gating decisions
`Digipeater` — digipeat repeat/block decisions
`Alert` — alert rules that triggered
`System` — general application events

callout.label: Why you may see "transmit" events with TX disabled
callout.text: Entries like `PacketTransmitBlocked` or `BeaconGenerated` are normal and expected. They record that the app *prepared* something and the safety gate *stopped* it from reaching the air. A generated beacon is not a transmitted one — the log is showing you the guardrail working, not a transmission.

blocks.p: The **Clear** button at the top right empties the in-memory event list so you can start watching fresh — handy right before you plug in a radio or start a __replay__ so only new activity shows. Clearing affects the on-screen list; it does not erase any log files already written to disk.
For a live health check of the radio link itself, open **Tools ▸ RF Diagnostics**. Instead of a line-by-line history, it shows summary tiles and warning panels that update as packets arrive.

bullets: **Tiles** across the top: **Packets** (total heard), **RF**, **APRS-IS**, **Duplicates**, and **Stations** (unique callsigns).
**Station Rates** and **Source Rates** — which stations and which sources are the busiest.
**Path Warnings** and **Beacon Warnings** — flags for questionable digipeater paths and stations beaconing too often.
**Recent packets** — a scrolling list showing each packet's time, callsign, source, duplicate state, link state, path, and any warnings.
A **Last updated** line and a **Clear** button to reset the counters.

blocks.screenshot: The RF Diagnostics window: a row of count tiles (Packets, RF, APRS-IS, Duplicates, Stations), a line summarizing link health, four small panels (Station Rates, Source Rates, Path Warnings, Beacon Warnings), and a scrolling recent-packets list at the bottom.

blocks.p: APRS Command keeps its data under one folder in your user profile. On Windows the default root is `%AppData%\APRS Command`. The exact paths for your machine are shown on the **First Run** setup screen, which lists **Application data**, **Logs**, **Map cache**, and **Exports** folders — the same folder review you saw the first time you launched the app.

rows: General application logs, including `startup-error.log` if the app ever fails to start.
Decoded-event log files, when file logging is turned on.

callout.label: File logging is off by default
callout.text: The Events window always keeps a live in-memory history (the most recent several thousand events). Writing those events to files in the `event-logs` folder is a separate, off-by-default option — the on-screen log works whether or not files are being written.

callout.label: If the app will not start
callout.text: When APRS Command fails during startup it writes the reason to `startup-error.log` in the `logs` folder (or your system temp folder as a last resort). That file has the timestamp and error text to include if you need to ask for help.

bullets: **The events list is empty.** Nothing has been decoded yet, or a filter is hiding everything. Set every dropdown back to `All` and clear both text boxes; then confirm a source is connected (a port, APRS-IS, or a running replay/simulation).
**I see lots of `PacketTransmitBlocked` events.** That is expected with transmit disabled — the app built a packet and the safety gate stopped it. It is the guardrail working, not an error.

**RF Diagnostics shows zero packets.** Your station is not hearing anything. Check that your TNC/radio port is connected (look for `PortConnected` in the events log) or that APRS-IS is connected, then watch the **Packets** tile climb as traffic arrives.

**Duplicate count is high.** Normal in busy areas or when both RF and APRS-IS carry the same stations; the **Duplicates** tile and each packet's duplicate state show what is being seen more than once.
**I get Beacon Warnings for a station.** That station is beaconing more often than recommended — informational only; APRS Command does not stop other stations.
**The event-logs folder is empty.** File logging is off by default; the on-screen log still works. Turn on file logging in settings if you want events written to disk.
**The app would not start and there is no window to check.** Open `startup-error.log` in the `logs` folder under `%AppData%\APRS Command` (or your temp folder) for the recorded error.
